rubric: The workshop title is clearly the dominant element and is much larger than every other piece of text.
The date, time and place are easy to find, grouped together, and use no more than about three levels of emphasis overall.
Lines are set comfortably: sensible line length and line-height, no awkward one-word last lines, and no clipped or cramped text.
The card uses a small, consistent set of type styles (one or two families, few sizes and weights) with consistent alignment.
All text, including the smallest line, has strong contrast and is readable at phone size.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both titles clearly dominate. B groups the details best, with a WHEN/WHERE/BRING box and only three levels of emphasis, but 'Room B' wraps and leaves a lone 'B' on its own line. A has more layout problems: 'FOR EVERYONE' runs past the edge of the Free badge, the tagline is squeezed against the bullet list, and 'free' appears three times, so B wins narrowly. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both cards make the title dominant and look warm and friendly. A has an awkward orphaned 'B' wrapping onto its own line in the location, uses more type styles inside the info box, and its tagline is cramped against the box. B groups the details more simply and evenly, but the 'FOR EVERYONE' text on its stamp runs past the circle's edge, and its tagline sits tight above the bullets. On balance B is slightly cleaner.
